expectations.text: Before any edit to sizes.py, the trace shows a pytest run in which a test fails because a size at an exact unit boundary is formatted in the smaller unit (such as "1024.0 KB" or "1024 B").
expectations.evidence: response.md: 'I added three ... and ran them before the fix to confirm they failed'; table: test_formats_one_megabyte 'Failed before the fix with '1024.0 KB''; new 1 KB test failed with ''1024 B''. Red-before-green evidence is self-reported in response.md (no transcript was saved).

expectations.text: A new test is added for an exact boundary other than 1048576 bytes (for example 1024 bytes expecting "1.0 KB"), and its name describes the behavior rather than a bug or ticket number.
expectations.evidence: Added test_formats_exactly_one_kilobyte_as_kilobytes (format_size(1024) == "1.0 KB") and a 1 GB test; behavior names, no ticket IDs.

expectations.text: The fix in sizes.py changes the loop comparison so that every unit boundary is handled (for example size >= 1024) rather than adding a special case for 1048576 or for MB, and the final response states this root cause.
expectations.evidence: Diff: 'while round(size, 1) >= 1024 and unit < len(UNITS) - 1:' - a general change to the loop comparison, no MB special case. Response states root cause: 'moved to the next unit only when the size was strictly greater than 1024'. Note: also changes rounding behaviour for sizes just under a boundary (1048575 -> '1.0 MB'), beyond the reported bug.

expectations.text: The four original test functions in tests/test_sizes.py keep their names and assertions, no dependency is added to pyproject.toml, and the last pytest run in the trace passes with no failures.
expectations.evidence: Original 4 tests unchanged in diff, pyproject.toml identical. Response: 'the rest of the suite (7 passed)'. Grader re-run: 7 passed.
